chapters.label: The opportunity
chapters.title: Quote in the conversation.
chapters.intro: Help buyers understand the equipment. Help PAC build and explain the right proposal.
chapters.detail: Two independent local demos: a product Website and a Sales Workspace for scope, configuration, review and customer discussion.
chapters.takeaway: Start with PAC’s priority: a quoting system and proposals the team can present with confidence.
chapters.caption: Captured seller proposal · Two alternatives for an illustrative customer. Independent customer access uses a separate recipient link.

proof.label: Sales Workspace
proof.title: Explain the equipment choice.
proof.body: Compare shared scope, added options and the price difference.
proof.caption: Captured seller proposal · V1, A and B at Rev 0. Illustrative customer; equipment prices in USD. Customer access uses a separate recipient link.

proof.label: Website
proof.title: Make the equipment easier to understand.
proof.body: Explore the application, equipment and questions that matter.
proof.caption: Captured Website buyer view · Homepage studio image is AI-assisted; original equipment photographs are available in product details.

chapters.label: PAC’s sales priorities
chapters.title: Build structure into the sales conversation.
chapters.intro: PAC’s priority: quote live, review before release, and present a clear equipment choice.
chapters.detail: PAC wants a higher win rate and a shorter time to close. Make scope, equipment choices and review part of one repeatable sales process.
steps: Configure options or an engineering requirement
Present alternatives and agree the customer’s next decision
chapters.takeaway: Evaluate the Sales Workspace first. The Website supports equipment understanding as a separate experience.
chapters.caption: Reported baseline from PAC discovery · Preparation time and customer turnaround are different measures.

artifacts.name: Sales Workspace
artifacts.title: Build, review and present.
artifacts.body: Capture the application. Configure and review the quote. Explain the options, price difference and next decision.

artifacts.name: Website
artifacts.title: Understand before asking.
artifacts.body: Use product context, relevant media and the reference Explorer to help buyers bring a useful application question.

chapters.label: The buyer experience
chapters.title: A better-informed equipment conversation.
chapters.intro: Help buyers understand what to ask before they discuss their application with PAC.
chapters.detail: The Website is a separate experience: product context, equipment media and an inquiry with a useful reference. It does not automatically create the prepared sales deal.

proof.label: Product context
proof.title: Make the equipment tangible.
proof.body: Show the product and its application before asking the visitor to submit an inquiry.
proof.caption: Captured Website preview · The homepage uses a labeled AI-assisted studio visualization; original equipment photographs are in product details.

proof.label: Explore
proof.title: Let the buyer point to a question.
proof.body: Explore a component or motion, then use that view to explain the question.
proof.caption: Captured Website preview · The crank-slider assembly demonstrates interaction. It is not PAC equipment or approved PAC CAD.

proof.label: Ask
proof.title: Keep the inquiry in context.
proof.body: Carry the selected view and application question into the Website inquiry.
proof.caption: Captured Website preview · Inquiry is independent from the Sales Workspace; PAC email routing and CRM integration are not connected.

chapters.takeaway: Website preview: product understanding and clearer questions. The quoting trial below focuses on the separate Sales Workspace.

chapters.label: The sales workspace
chapters.title: From a clear proposal to a confident next step.
chapters.intro: One deal holds the alternatives, configuration, published versions and customer discussion.
chapters.detail: Present the equipment alternatives, then show the application, configuration and required review behind them. Use revision history as proof that issued work is preserved.

proof.label: Customer proposal
proof.title: Explain the choice.
proof.body: Bring application context, equipment, scope and price into one proposal. Compare alternatives and keep questions tied to the published version.
proof.caption: Captured seller proposal · V1, A and B at Rev 0. The recipient link opens the same published scope with customer feedback.

proof.label: Saved revision
proof.title: Respond with the scope in view.
proof.body: A customer requests a Spare Parts Kit for Alternative B. Add the option to a new revision and save it before review and publication.
proof.caption: Captured rehearsal · Alternative B, Rev 1 draft with a $1,130 Spare Parts Kit. Draft changes are separate from the published proposal.

proof.label: Published proposal
proof.title: Publish the change. Preserve the record.
proof.body: In this sample, Alternative B moves from $40,810 to $41,940. Proposal V1 remains at its original price; the customer can review the new published version.
proof.caption: Captured rehearsal · Proposal V2, Alternative B. Sample equipment prices in USD; these are not Annora subscription prices.

chapters.takeaway: Working local demonstration: configuration, save, revision, review and publication. PAC’s production identity, integrations and approval policy remain to be agreed.

chapters.label: The trial scope
chapters.title: Your scenarios. Two weeks. A clear evaluation.
chapters.intro: A working trial of quoting, presenting and responding to customers, with guided setup and a joint results review.
chapters.detail: Proposed starting scope — to be agreed with PAC before the trial begins.

scope.body: Confirm the Rollbag family, price source and option rules.
Name the sales users and the reviewer who will evaluate the work.
Cover standard options, an engineering requirement, review and a customer decision.

deliverables: A usable evaluation environment for the agreed product family
3–5 completed quote cases and a reviewed comparison of alternatives
Configuration, price and lead-time checks; a shared scorecard and remaining gaps
chapters.boundary: The Website remains a separate review preview. A full Website rollout, additional machine families and new integrations require an agreed scope. Approved PAC CAD is not a prerequisite for this quoting trial.
chapters.takeaway: Day 1 starts when the environment, access, source cases and participants are ready.

chapters.label: The evaluation
chapters.title: Agree the test. Observe the work.
chapters.intro: Use matched quoting cases and a shared scorecard, then decide together.

timeline.title: Get ready
timeline.body: Confirm access, cases, pricing sources, users, success criteria and the decision date.

timeline.title: Set the baseline
timeline.body: Walk through the workflow and measure current quote preparation on matched cases.

timeline.title: Use the workflow
timeline.body: Begin with guided tasks, then let PAC users repeat the work with less assistance.

timeline.title: Review together
timeline.body: Review results and gaps. Agree whether to continue and what paid use would cover.

scorecard.name: Complete the work
scorecard.check: PAC users complete their assigned core tasks without Annora operating the interface. Record help and blockers.

scorecard.name: Match approved sources
scorecard.check: Required scope, options, prices and lead times reconcile with PAC’s approved references.

scorecard.name: Control release
scorecard.check: Unpriced engineering work remains non-final; required approval identifies the reviewer before release.

scorecard.name: Preserve the record
scorecard.check: The requested change appears in a new revision; earlier issued proposals remain unchanged.

chapters.takeaway: Agree pass criteria before Day 1. Compare task time, assistance and reviewer understanding; measure turnaround separately.

chapters.label: The continuation decision
chapters.title: Prove the workflow. Earn continued use.
chapters.intro: Two weeks free. Paid use begins only after we both confirm scope, price and support in writing. No automatic charges.
chapters.offerTerms: Paid use begins only after we both confirm scope, price and support in writing.
chapters.detail: Evaluate real quoting work, then decide whether the results justify an ongoing service.
service: Sales Workspace access for the agreed users
Agreed product, pricing, lead-time and option-rule coverage
Proposal history, review responsibility and follow-up
decisions: Choose the product family, PAC-approved sources, cases and trial owner.
Confirm the participants, approval rules, ready-to-use environment and results-review date.
Agree success criteria, unresolved blockers and the proposed paid scope, pricing basis and support.
Confirm data export, retention and access if PAC stops.
chapters.boundary: The Website is a separate preview. Rollout, CRM, SSO, email, documents, signing and payment need agreed scope and readiness checks.
chapters.takeaway: Day 1 starts when access, source data, participants and the agreed workflow are ready.
chapters.scope: Proposed: one product family · 2–3 PAC participants · 3–5 quote cases

trialRows.title: Standard quote
trialRows.output: Saved quote and PDF: scope, options, price and lead time.
trialRows.accept: Required information is complete. Options, prices and lead times match PAC’s approved sources.

trialRows.title: Engineering / special
trialRows.output: Reason, hours, materials and delivery conditions.
trialRows.accept: Unpriced work stays non-final. Returned work is resubmitted; authorized review is recorded before release.

trialRows.title: Customer decision
trialRows.output: Alternatives, feedback and a revised proposal.
trialRows.accept: PAC users explain the price difference and record feedback. Earlier issued versions stay unchanged.

chapters.trialResult: PAC operates the agreed tasks. We review completed cases, source checks, assistance needed and remaining gaps.

value.title: Repeat a reliable sales process
value.body: Scope, configuration and review stay together, from one rep and one quote to the next.

value.title: Keep product knowledge current
value.body: PAC maintains agreed prices and rules, with defined Annora support and maintenance.

value.title: Keep the decision moving
value.body: The buyer’s next decision and PAC’s internal follow-up stay distinct, with the right proposal history.
